findings.summary: The living security-decision doc still states 'không cần view SECURITY DEFINER nào cho đường đọc' for secret_box_openings — directly contradicted by migration 0015, which adds exactly that view. Migration 0015's own header says it 'REVERSES' this doc and points to plans/260910-1951-screen-audit-spec-test-gaps/spec/system/permissions.md, but that plan-scoped copy was never merged into the real docs/ tree (git status confirms docs/vi/system/permissions.md is unmodified on this branch). A future reader of the canonical doc — the one place this project's security posture is supposed to be recorded — will be told something false about a privacy-sensitive read path.

recent_gift_recipients does ORDER BY s.opened_at DESC LIMIT 10 over secret_box_openings with no index on opened_at (0011 only indexes user_id). Currently a full sort on an append-only log; cheap while the table is small, becomes a real per-request cost as openings accumulate since /kudos is a public, unauthenticated, presumably high-traffic page. Fix: CREATE INDEX idx_secret_box_openings_opened_at ON public.secret_box_openings (opened_at DESC).

A transport failure (network error, action throws) on toggleKudoHeart is swallowed silently with only a comment — pendingIds clears via finally so the button un-wedges, but the user gets no visible signal the toggle failed (no toast, unlike other kudos actions which do use useKudosToast). This is a UX gap, not a correctness bug: the card state stays consistent with the server, and the design note explicitly frames it as deliberate (not optimistic). Worth a toast on catch in a follow-up, not blocking.
